meta.title: How we charge — Edura
meta.description: Edura's commission model explained with a real worked example: the platform's share, settlement timing, online and cash payment, and what we never charge.

hero.title: How we charge
hero.subtitle: Every pound in Edura has a known path before it moves. This page explains the model in numbers, not adjectives.
hero.note: The rates in these examples are read from the platform's own settings right now — they are not written into this page.

principles.title: Three rules govern every transaction
principles.p1title: What the student pays is the price
principles.p1body: Nothing is added on top of a lesson or subscription price. The platform's share is deducted from the lesson itself, after the money has come in.
principles.p2title: Rates freeze when the class is created
principles.p2body: A class records its rates the moment it is created, and keeps them. If the platform or the center changes pricing later, running classes are never re-rated — the change applies to new classes only.
principles.p3title: Every pound leaves an entry that cannot be edited
principles.p3body: Each settlement writes entries into a ledger that is closed against updates and deletes at the database level. Not even a super-admin account can alter an entry once written.

cases.title: Three situations, three calculations
cases.intro: These examples are computed by the very same functions that settle real money in the system. The inputs (subscription price, lesson price, number of attendees) are illustrative — the rates are read from platform settings.

a.title: A student subscribes directly to a teacher
a.body: No center is involved, so there is no center share. The platform takes its commission at payment time, and the remainder lands in the teacher's wallet in the same moment.
a.settled: Settled the moment the payment succeeds — online or cash.

b.title: A teacher teaches in a center's hall
b.body: The lesson price splits three ways at published rates: platform, teacher, center. The calculation runs per student who actually attended, and whatever remains after the platform and center shares goes to the teacher exactly — no rounding leaks.
b.settled: Settled when the session is closed — attendance is what counts.
b.unconfigured: The platform has not configured a default hall split yet, so this example is unavailable right now.

c.title: A center class without a configured hall rate
c.body: If a class was created without hall pricing, it settles on the platform's flat fee per attending student — with no center share, because no agreed rate exists to compute one from.
c.settled: Settled when the session is closed.
c.note: The flat fee never exceeds the lesson's own value — if a lesson is cheaper than the fee, the fee is capped at the price and the teacher's net can never go negative.

cases.method2Title: A fourth shape: a center share per attending student
cases.method2Body: Some halls are priced as a fixed amount (or a percentage of the lesson price) per attending student instead of a share of the whole room. The center sets its own hall's rate in that case, capped by the platform's published rate, and the teacher sees the number on the hall card before booking — not after settlement. There is no published default for this shape: it is configured per hall.

timing.title: When the money reaches you
timing.t1body: Independent-teacher subscription: the moment payment succeeds. Center class: the moment the session is closed, and only for students marked present. A counter check-in without the second check-in at the hall door (in two-stage mode) does not count as attendance, and therefore does not settle.
timing.t2body: The net lands in your wallet as it is earned. Every entry names the session and the student behind it.
timing.t3body: You request a payout from your available balance, and the request reserves that amount immediately so it cannot be requested twice. It is then reviewed and paid. There is no minimum and no withdrawal fee.

methods.title: Online and cash — one ledger
methods.onlineBody: Card or mobile wallet through Paymob. The amount always comes from the server-side intent, never from a number sent by the browser, and the confirmation is verified against a cryptographic signature before a single pound moves.
methods.cashBody: Center staff record the payment at the counter and issue a numbered receipt. Cash is written to the same ledger with the same entries as an online payment — there is no second money path.
methods.note: The payment method changes neither the calculation nor the distribution. All that changes is who recorded it.

noHidden.title: What we don't charge
noHidden.b1: No monthly platform subscription for a center or a teacher.
noHidden.b3: No fee for withdrawing your own wallet balance.
noHidden.b4: Nothing charged to the student on top of the lesson or subscription price.
noHidden.b5: No commission on a session nobody attended — the calculation starts at attendance.

hero.title: The questions we hear most
hero.subtitle: If yours isn't here, the help center goes deeper and we're one message away.

faq.moreBody: The help center has the long form, and if you need a person, contact us.

items.a1: A share of the lesson or subscription value, deducted after the money comes in — not a monthly fee and not a setup fee. The «How we charge» page has the full worked example at the platform's current rates.
items.q2: When does money reach my wallet?
items.a2: An independent teacher's subscription settles the moment payment succeeds. A center class settles when the session is closed, and only for the students whose attendance was recorded.
items.a3: Any time, from your available balance. The request reserves the amount immediately so it cannot be requested twice, then it is reviewed and paid. No minimum, no withdrawal fee.
items.a4: Center staff record the payment at the counter and issue a numbered receipt, and it is written to the same ledger with the same entries as an online payment.
items.q5: What if a student checks in at the counter but never enters the hall?
items.a5: In two-stage mode a counter check-in on its own is recorded as a distinct state that does not count as attendance, and it is flagged plainly to the teacher. Because it is not attendance, that lesson does not settle for that student.
items.a6: Everything you can do except the wallet, payouts, financial settings, and managing assistants. Every action is recorded under their name and marked as done on your behalf.
items.q7: Can a parent see their child's messages?
items.a7: They can see their minor child's threads with adults, read-only, without touching read receipts. Both sides see a permanent notice that the oversight is active — there is no hidden monitoring.
items.q8: How is my center's data protected from other centers?
items.a8: Isolation is enforced in the database itself, not only in the screens. A request from one center cannot read a row belonging to another, even if someone tried.
items.a9: Yes, straight from the browser with no install, and it can be added to the home screen as an app. Attendance keeps working when the connection drops and syncs when it returns.
items.q10: Can I try it before paying?
items.a10: Signing up is free and needs no card. The platform's share only begins at the first real payment — if no money moved, there is no commission.
